messages.content: Could you retrieve the current weather data for New York, specifically focusing on the temperature?.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function `requests_get` with appropriate params.

Open-Meteo API requires lat/lon. For NYC approximate lat=40.7128, lon=-74.0060. We want temperature. Probably we can ask for "current_weather=true". But the tool signature only includes query params: latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't have other options like current_weather. However maybe the base endpoint will return some defaults? Let's check typical usage: open-meteo.com/api?latitude=...&longitude=... returns hourly etc. To get current temp, use &hourly=temperature_2m or &current_weather=true. Since our function signature does not allow arbitrary extra params except those defined. So can't specify current_weather param. Maybe we just fetch basic forecast which might include daily temperatures but not real-time. Alternatively we could still pass additional params via the generic params object? It's typed as {latitude?, longitude?, elevation?}. Only those keys allowed. So cannot add others. That seems limiting. Perhaps the tool expects us to provide full URL including all needed query strings manually. Because url parameter accepts entire URL. Then params may override? Usually if you supply both url and params, they combine. But we can embed everything into url itself. Eg: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=40.7128&longitude=-74.0060&current_weather=true".

Thus set url accordingly. Provide headers optional. We'll do minimal.

Let's craft JSON:

{
"url": "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=40.7128&longitude=-74.0060&current_weather=true",
"headers": {},
"timeout": 10.0,
"params": {}, 
...

But we don't need many fields. Just required ones: url, headers optional, timeout optional, params empty. Also allow_redirects default true.

We'll produce function call.
